caption: Apparent sizes are read from the ladder and hold to about 5-10% between gels. Heights are fractions of a saturated pixel on the same image. 'Best guess' is the claim; its footnotes are the papers behind it. 'Show evidence' puts the lanes behind each claim on the plot and the gel strips, and lists every lane where the band is seen and where it isn't. Without footnotes, a guess rests on these gels alone.

evidence.text: Strep pull-down (Optimisation A, 04/11/26): one of only three bands streptavidin beads pulled out of lysate before any reaction; pre-clearing removed it almost completely.
Reaction drop-outs (Optimisation B, 04/11/26): still present when biotin-GPP is left out, so the biotin was already on it.
In mouse 3T3-L1 cells labelled with [³H]biotin, the biotin-containing subunit of ACC ran at about 220 kDa, and every labelled protein could be removed with avidin.
Mammals have two ACC forms, of about 265 kDa and 275-280 kDa, so an ACC band near 250 on this gel is within the expected range.
Lists ACC (cytoplasmic) as one of four endogenously biotinylated proteins of mammalian cells, and shows their levels differ between cell types.

bands.summary: Most likely acetyl-CoA carboxylase, the largest of the endogenously biotinylated carboxylases, already carrying biotin in the blood before any reaction. Confidence is high that it is endogenously biotinylated (streptavidin pulls it down and it needs no biotin-GPP) and moderate that it is ACC, which rests on size alone.

bands.before: No: not pulled down or cleared

evidence.text: Strep pull-down: absent from both bead eluates (≤0.004) and unchanged by pre-clearing (0.110 → 0.109), so it isn't a biotinylated blood protein.
Serial dilution (18/09/26): rises from 0.02 at 1 in 5 to about 0.08 at 1 in 100 and below, in both genotypes; it gets stronger, not weaker, as there is less blood.
Frozen blood (24/09/26) and RBC lysis (19/08/26): the same direction, stronger at 1 in 50 and with 3x lysis (less protein).
The lysate seems to suppress it: it is weakest where there is most blood.

bands.summary: Probably a component of the reaction mix rather than a blood protein: it is not pulled down before the reaction and gets stronger as the lysate is diluted. Confidence is moderate, since the behaviour holds on three gels but no reaction-only (no-lysate) control has been run to confirm it.

evidence.text: Strep pull-down: the strongest of the three bead-eluate bands (0.47 at 1 in 2); pre-clearing removed about 40% of it from the lysate.
Reaction drop-outs: still present with no biotin-GPP.
The biotinylated PC subunit ran at about 120 kDa in mouse cells.

In human fibroblasts PC gives a biotinylated band at 128 kDa, and that biotinylation falls to about a tenth in cells lacking holocarboxylase synthetase, the enzyme that puts biotin on carboxylases: genetic evidence that the band is a carboxylase.
A strong ~125 kDa streptavidin band was purified and sequenced (Edman) and turned out to be pyruvate carboxylase. This was in bacteria, but it is a direct identification rather than one by size.
A widely used protocol expects untreated control lanes on streptavidin blots to show only endogenous biotinylated bands at 130, 75 and 72 kDa.
Carboxylase activity is routinely measured in blood lymphocytes, so white cells carry these enzymes.

Mature red cells have no mitochondria, where PC sits, so in whole blood this band should report white cells and platelets rather than red cells (textbook reasoning, not checked against a source here).

bands.summary: Most likely pyruvate carboxylase, an endogenously biotinylated mitochondrial enzyme carried by white cells and platelets rather than red cells. Confidence is high that it is endogenously biotinylated and moderate to high that it is PC: the size matches and PC has been identified directly at this size elsewhere, though not in these samples.

evidence.text: Strep pull-down: in both bead eluates (0.36 at 1 in 2); pre-clearing removed about 40%.
Reaction drop-outs: 0.05-0.08 with no biotin-GPP, the same as with the full reaction.
MCC and PCC biotinylated subunits ran at about 75 and 72 kDa in mouse cells; at this gel's resolution they would merge into one band.
PCC (72 kDa) and MCC (76 kDa) run as a doublet on streptavidin blots of fibroblasts, and lose their biotin when holocarboxylase synthetase is missing.
In mouse tissue, ~75 and ~150 kDa bands appeared with the avidin conjugate alone, in every sample; the authors attribute them to MCC/PCC and PC but did not identify them.
Background bands at about 72, 75 and 150 kDa are described as the usual signature of endogenous biotin in streptavidin westerns.
PCC activity is measured in blood lymphocytes: white cells carry these mitochondrial carboxylases.

bands.summary: Most likely the biotinylated α subunits of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase and propionyl-CoA carboxylase (about 75 and 72 kDa), running together as one band. Confidence is high that it is endogenously biotinylated and moderate that it is MCC/PCC, which rests on size and on these being the known biotinylated proteins of this size.

bands.guess: Blood protein labelled without the enzymes

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs: 0.07-0.08 with no REP1 or no RabGGTase II, but 0.00-0.01 with no biotin-GPP.
Strep pull-down: not in the bead eluates, so not biotinylated in the blood.
Frozen blood: 0.13 neat, 0.03 at 1 in 10, 0 at 1 in 50, so it comes from the blood.
Could be the lysate's own prenyltransferases, or labelling without an enzyme.

bands.summary: A blood protein that picks up the biotin label without the added enzymes, perhaps through the lysate's own prenyltransferases or by non-enzymatic attachment. Confidence in what it is is low: it needs biotin-GPP and fades with dilution, but nothing here identifies it.

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs: 0.06-0.11 with the full reaction or without REP1; 0.00-0.01 without RabGGTase II; 0.02 without biotin-GPP.
Serial dilution: 0.04 at 1 in 5 rising to about 0.10 at 1 in 1000 and 1 in 10 000, in both genotypes.
Strep pull-down: absent from the bead eluates and unchanged by clearing.
The lysate seems to suppress it: it is weakest where there is most blood. Possibly a labelled recombinant protein or contaminant.

bands.summary: Probably labelled reagent, a recombinant protein or contaminant in the reaction mix that RabGGTase II attaches biotin-GPP to. Confidence is moderate: it needs the enzyme and biotin-GPP but not REP1, and it gets stronger rather than weaker as the blood is diluted away, but a no-lysate control is needed to confirm it.

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs (no defect): 0.15 full, 0.06 without REP1, 0.05 without RabGGTase II, 0.00 without biotin-GPP.
Frozen blood: 0.02-0.05 across neat, 1 in 10 and 1 in 50.
Strep pull-down: not in the eluates; 0.20 vs 0.17 before and after clearing.

bands.summary: An unidentified product of the labelling reaction that depends on biotin-GPP and partly on the added enzymes. Confidence in any identity is low, and because it changes little between genotypes or with dilution it is unlikely to report the prenylation defect.

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs (defect): 0.09 full; 0.03 without REP1, 0.00 without RabGGTase II, 0.03 without biotin-GPP.
Defect vs no defect: 0.09 vs 0.06 (drop-outs), 0.05 vs 0.02 (RBC lysis 1x), 0.04 vs 0.02 (frozen blood, neat).
Strep pull-down: not in the eluates; 0.24 vs 0.31 before and after clearing.
Could be a second substrate (a larger Rab?) or an SDS-resistant Rab complex.

bands.summary: A product of the full prenylation reaction that is stronger with the defect, possibly a second, larger Rab-family substrate or an SDS-resistant complex of the ~25 kDa Rabs. Confidence is low to moderate: it needs all three components, but it is weak, sits beside a saturated band, and a small peak is also measured without biotin-GPP.

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs: 0.62 (no defect) and saturated (defect) with the full reaction; 0.00-0.07 without RabGGTase II or biotin-GPP; without REP1, 0.02 (no defect) but 0.37 (defect).
Defect lanes are saturated on every gel at the higher lysate amounts; serial dilution 1 in 100: 0.21 (defect) vs 0.01 (no defect).
Strep pull-down: absent from the bead eluates, so made in the reaction.

The same kind of in vitro prenylation assay, with mass spectrometry, detected unprenylated Rab GTPases (including Rab7A, Rab14 and Rab1A) accumulating in cells from patients with mevalonate kinase deficiency.

In blood mononuclear cells from six patients with mevalonate kinase deficiency, the assay showed a clear build-up of unprenylated Rab proteins compared with heterozygous carriers and healthy controls.
Which Rabs make up this band in mouse blood is not checked against the literature; Rab27 was suggested earlier from size only.

Higher with the defect could mean more unprenylated Rab, or simply more Rab in the sample: nothing here measures total Rab. The lysate has its own REP, which is why leaving out REP1 only partly removes the band.

bands.summary: Most likely unprenylated Rab GTPases labelled in the reaction, the signal this assay is designed to measure, and much stronger in blood with the prenylation defect. Confidence is high that these are Rab-like reaction products and moderate about why they differ, because more total Rab in the defect samples would give the same result as more unprenylated Rab.

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs (defect): 0.37 full; 0.02 without REP1, without RabGGTase II or without biotin-GPP.
Defect vs no defect: 0.37 vs 0.05 (drop-outs), 0.20 vs 0.00 (serial dilution 1 in 5), 0.06-0.12 vs 0.00-0.01 (frozen blood, neat).
Strep pull-down: not in the eluates.
Could be a smaller Rab-like substrate, or a fragment of the ~25 band.

bands.summary: A Rab-like reaction product that, like the ~25 kDa band, needs REP1, RabGGTase II and biotin-GPP and is seen mostly with the defect. Confidence is moderate that it is a prenylation substrate and low about its identity: it could be a smaller GTPase or a breakdown fragment of the ~25 kDa Rabs.

evidence.text: Reaction drop-outs: 0.04-0.07 in every lane, too weak to say what it needs.
Defect vs no defect: 0.22 vs 0.01 (serial dilution 1 in 5), 0.11-0.14 vs 0.03-0.04 (frozen blood, neat).

bands.summary: A small labelled species seen mainly in samples with the defect, of unknown identity. Confidence is low: it is too weak on the drop-out gel to say which reaction components it needs, so it could be a substrate or a fragment.
